org.name: Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

hazard: Lack of early involvement of approved social worker

reports.title: Leah Ratheram
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Adults aged between 18 - 25 now have mental health services provided by two organisations - Forward Thinking Birmingham and Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health Trust. If a patient presents in crisis to A&E they will be seen by someone from the RAID team who work for Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health Trust. If they require ongoing treatment they will be referred to forward Thinking Birmingham. There is a concern that patients will have no coordinated approach to their care at a time of crisis
concerns.hazard: lack of coordinated care for young adults

concerns.quote: Both organisations use different record keeping systems. There is a real risk that information will not be shared effectively and key risk factors will be missed in the handover process. It was unclear how staff from each organisation would access each other's records when patients present to one or other of the services.

The Mental Health Act assessment process was followed in this case was unclear. An approved social worked declined to be involved until the assessment had been completed. There is a concern that lack of involvement of this speciality at any early stage will affect the quality of mental health act assessments and the safety of patients.
concerns.hazard: lack of early involvement of approved social worker

reports.title: Richard Carlon
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

concerns.quote: No approved Mental Health practitioner was available to make the Mental Health Act assessment of Mr Carlon on 14/11/18. I was told this was an ongoing problem and was delaying assessments.
concerns.hazard: lack of approved mental health practitioner for assessment

concerns.quote: When Mr Carlon was found safe and well at home WMP did not advise BSMHT. This was a missed opportunity for Mental health to re‐engage with Mr Carlon and make a further assessment of his condition. Consideration need to be given to how agencies can improve communication.
concerns.hazard: failure to notify mental health team after safe check

reports.title: Matthew Lynch: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

promises.quote: The review acknowledged the risk of relapse identified in May 2023 on page 14, identifying that whilst plans were made within the Multi-disciplinary Team, there was no clear process to track these actions, leading to a lack of oversight. If there had been stronger oversight, the team would have been aware of the non-compliance with medication sooner, allowing for timely intervention. This would have included tracking the perpetrator's prescription. To address this, the team has now implemented a
promises.summary: Implement actions tracker for oversight of agreed plans

concerns.quote: internal investigation did not address how and whether the offender's use of medication should have been monitored after the clinic visit on 12/05/23
concerns.hazard: lack of medication monitoring after clinic visit
